anomalies.observed: R21 (10k) is a pull resistor on the gate node of T7 (IRLR2905, main-pump low-side switch). Its pin 2 is on +3V3 and pin 1 is on /NET0062. That gate node is therefore pulled up to 3.3 V, not to GND. The equivalent gate-pull resistor R31 on the T1 gate is correctly returned to GND.
anomalies.expected: A gate pull-down on a low-side N-MOSFET should return to GND, so that the pump switch defaults to OFF when the driver pins are floating or during boot. Returning it to +3V3 defaults the pump to ON.
anomalies.impact: The main circulation pump gate is held high through 10k whenever T4 is off and IO10 is not actively pulling low. The pump can turn on unintentionally at power-up or if the GPIO floats, which is a safety-relevant failure.

anomalies.observed: The TPS62933 buck regulator U3 has its EN pin (pin 2) explicitly marked no-connect, so the enable input is left floating.
anomalies.expected: The EN pin of a TPS62933 should be tied to VIN (directly or through a divider) or driven by a GPIO, because a floating enable leaves the 24 V-to-5 V converter's state undefined.

evidence.quote: U1 — TPS62933 (TI) | 24 V → 5 V synchronous buck regulator, 3 A

anomalies.impact: The 5 V rail that powers the ESP32 and the LDO may not start reliably, or may not start at all, since the enable is not defined.

parsed.summary: The main anomaly is R21, a gate pull resistor on the main-pump MOSFET T7 that returns to +3V3 instead of GND, which would leave the pump on by default. A lower-confidence second issue is that the TPS62933 enable pin is left unconnected.
